translationRepairs: During the Dazhun era he rose to commander of cavalry and infantry and, together with Li Cunxiao, attacked Zhang Jun's forces at Pingyang.
During the Dashun era he rose to commander of cavalry and infantry and, together with Li Cunxiao, attacked Zhang Jun's forces at Pingyang.
大順 is the Dashun reign period; Dazhun is a mistransliteration in the idiomatic field.
In the Dazhun era he was repeatedly promoted to commander of horse and foot, and with Li Cunxiao struck Zhang Jun's army at Pingyang.
In the Dashun era he was repeatedly promoted to commander of horse and foot, and with Li Cunxiao struck Zhang Jun's army at Pingyang.
The literal field repeats the same mistransliteration of 大順, whose standard pinyin is Dashun.

In the second year of Dazhun the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign east of the mountains and appointed Cunxin commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot. Cunxiao flew into a rage. The Martial Emperor sent Cunzhi to take the post in his place, whereupon Cunxiao began plotting rebellion.

In the second year of Dashun, the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign east of the mountains and appointed Cunxin commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot. Cunxiao flew into a rage. The Martial Emperor sent Cunzhi to take the post in his place, whereupon Cunxiao began plotting rebellion.
大順二年 is the second year of Dashun. The revised replacement also supplies the comma required after the introductory date.

In the second year of Dazhun the Martial Emperor made a great expedition to seize territory in Shandong, appointing Cunxin as commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot; when Cunxiao heard of it he was angry; the Martial Emperor had Cunzhi replace him, and Cunxiao then plotted rebellion.

In the second year of Dashun, the Martial Emperor made a great expedition to seize territory in Shandong, appointing Cunxin as commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot; when Cunxiao heard of it he was angry; the Martial Emperor had Cunzhi replace him, and Cunxiao then plotted rebellion.
The literal field also mistransliterates 大順 and needs a comma after the introductory date.
Cunxin drew his troops back but was worsted by the Wei forces, abandoned his baggage, and fell back to Ming Prefecture, losing perhaps a fifth of his army.
Cunxin drew his troops back but was worsted by the Wei forces, abandoned his baggage, and fell back to Ming Prefecture, losing twenty to thirty percent of his army.
十二三 means two or three tenths. The revised idiomatic wording states that range naturally rather than the inaccurate 'perhaps a fifth.'
When Zhang Jun marched additional forces against Taiyuan, a Luzhou junior officer named Feng Ba killed his commander Li Keong and turned the city in revolt.
When Zhang Jun marched additional forces against Taiyuan, a Luzhou junior officer named Feng Ba killed his commander Li Kegong and turned the city in revolt.
李克恭 is Li Kegong; Keong omits the consonant represented by 恭 (gong).
When Zhang Jun added troops against Taiyuan, a minor officer of Luzhou, Feng Ba, killed his commander Li Keong and rebelled with the city.
When Zhang Jun added troops against Taiyuan, a minor officer of Luzhou, Feng Ba, killed his commander Li Kegong and rebelled with the city.
The literal field has the same spelling error for 李克恭, correctly romanized Li Kegong.
That night the Bian general Li Dan broke camp and fled. Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, taking and killing enemies by the tens of thousands, then turned back to invest Luzhou.
That night the Bian general Li Dang broke camp and fled. Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, taking and killing enemies by the tens of thousands, then turned back to invest Luzhou.
The general is 李讜, whose given name is Dang, not Dan.
That night the Bian general Li Dan gathered his army and fled; Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, capturing and slaying tens of thousands, then withdrew to attack Luzhou.
That night the Bian general Li Dang gathered his army and fled; Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, capturing and slaying tens of thousands, then withdrew to attack Luzhou.
The literal field likewise requires Li Dang for 李讜.

In the third month of the second year of Dazhun, Xingzhou commissioner An Zhijian defected to the Bian army. The Martial Emperor sent Cunxiao to secure Xing and Ming and invested him with the commissioner's regalia.

In the third month of the second year of Dashun, Xingzhou commissioner An Zhijian defected to the Bian army. The Martial Emperor sent Cunxiao to secure Xing and Ming and invested him with the commissioner's regalia.
大順二年 is Dashun 2, so Dazhun in the idiomatic field is erroneous.

In the third month of the second year of Dazhun, An Zhijian, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, rebelled and entered the Bian army; the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to pacify Xing and Ming and thereby invested him with commission and regalia.

In the third month of the second year of Dashun, An Zhijian, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, rebelled and entered the Bian army; the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to pacify Xing and Ming and thereby invested him with commission and regalia.
The literal field repeats the same error; 大順 is Dashun.

In the third month of the first year of Qianning Cunxiao mounted the wall to confess his guilt and wept before the Martial Emperor: "I owed you deep kindness and rose to command armies. Had slanderers not driven us apart, why would I ever have forsaken a father's bond to join your enemies?!

In the third month of the first year of Qianning, Cunxiao mounted the wall to confess his guilt and wept before the Martial Emperor: "I owed you deep kindness and rose to command armies. Had slanderers not driven us apart, why would I ever have forsaken a father's bond to join your enemies?!
The Chinese places a pause after 乾寧元年三月; the comma prevents the English date from running into Cunxiao's name.
In the ninth month Wang Chuqiong marched out with his full strength, caught them unprepared, and burst upon the rampart gate.
In the ninth month Wang Chuqiu marched out with his full strength, caught them unprepared, and burst upon the rampart gate.
王處球 is Wang Chuqiu because 球 is qiu, not qiong.
In the ninth month Wang Chuqiong led out all his forces, taking advantage of their unreadiness, and suddenly reached the rampart gate.
In the ninth month Wang Chuqiu led out all his forces, taking advantage of their unreadiness, and suddenly reached the rampart gate.
The literal field has the same romanization error for 王處球, correctly Wang Chuqiu.
Zhixiang said, "Old companions from Fen and Pei meeting again here—what could bring greater joy!"
Zhixiang said, "Old companions from Feng and Pei meeting again here—what could bring greater joy!"
豐沛 is the paired place-name allusion Feng and Pei; Fen incorrectly imports 汾 from the preceding context.
In the eleventh year he was made prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shannan.
In the eleventh year he was made prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shanbei.
The office is explicitly 山北團練使, Shanbei training commissioner, not Shannan.
In the eleventh year he was appointed prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shannan.
In the eleventh year he was appointed prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shanbei.
The literal field also mistranslates 山北 as Shannan; Shanbei is the source reading.
